grammarPages.titleEnglish: Introduce Someone with 叫, 姓, and 是
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Introduce someone by name, surname, or identity.
grammarPages.explanation: 叫, 姓 and 是 are used as verbs and equate two nouns in a sentence. 姓 comes only before a family name. 叫 comes before a given name or a full name. 是 says what someone is. Put 不 before them to say no.

patternRows.english: His name is Zhongming.
Whose surname is Li?
He is not Taiwanese.

text.traditional: A：她是誰？ B：她是新同學。
text.simplified: A：她是谁？ B：她是新同学。
text.pinyin: A: Tā shì shéi? B: Tā shì xīn tóngxué.
text.english: A: Who is she? B: She is a new classmate.

text.traditional: 她是日本人，她不是台灣人。
text.simplified: 她是日本人，她不是台湾人。
text.pinyin: Tā shì Rìběn rén, tā bú shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: She is Japanese. She is not Taiwanese.

text.traditional: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
text.simplified: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
text.pinyin: Tā bú xìng Lǐ, tā xìng Xiǎolín, jiào Xiǎolín Yǒuměi.
text.english: Her surname is not Li. Her surname is Xiaolin; her name is Xiaolin Youmei.

items.question: Does 姓 take the full name too?
items.answer: 姓 takes only a family name; use 叫 before a given name or full name.

right.traditional: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
right.simplified: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
right.pinyin: Tā bú xìng Lǐ, tā xìng Xiǎolín, jiào Xiǎolín Yǒuměi.
right.english: Her surname is not Li. Her surname is Xiaolin; her name is Xiaolin Youmei.

items.question: Can 姓 introduce a given name?
items.answer: Use 叫 before the given name 中明; 姓 takes only a family name.

right.english: His name is Zhongming.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe Someone with 很 or 不
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that someone is or is not busy, tired, or pretty.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 很 or 不 before adjectives like 漂亮, 可愛, 忙 and 累. These words already carry the meaning of "is", so no 是 is needed. 很 can mean "very"; 不 means "not".

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Ask a Yes/No Question with 嗎
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Turn a statement into a yes-or-no question with one ending word.
grammarPages.explanation: Add 嗎 at the very end of the statement, without any change in order. Nothing inside the sentence moves. The listener answers yes or no.

patternRows.english: Is he Taiwanese?
Is she pretty?

text.traditional: A：他是日本人嗎？ B：他不是日本人，他是台灣人。
text.simplified: A：他是日本人吗？ B：他不是日本人，他是台湾人。
text.pinyin: A: Tā shì Rìběn rén ma? B: Tā bú shì Rìběn rén, tā shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: A: Is he Japanese? B: He is not Japanese; he is Taiwanese.

text.traditional: 高先生叫家樂嗎？
text.simplified: 高先生叫家乐吗？
text.pinyin: Gāo xiānsheng jiào Jiālè ma?
text.english: Is Mr. Gao called Jiale?

text.traditional: 他忙嗎？
text.simplified: 他忙吗？
text.pinyin: Tā máng ma?
text.english: Is he busy?

items.question: Where does 嗎 go?
items.answer: At the very end. The whole statement stays first, exactly in its order.

right.english: Is he Japanese?

items.question: Do I keep 嗎 when I answer?
items.answer: No. 嗎 only asks a question; the answer is the plain statement.

right.traditional: 他不是日本人，他是台灣人。
right.simplified: 他不是日本人，他是台湾人。
right.pinyin: Tā bú shì Rìběn rén, tā shì Táiwān rén.
right.english: He is not Japanese; he is Taiwanese.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 呢 to Say “And You?”
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask the same question back with 呢, without repeating the whole sentence.
grammarPages.explanation: When a question is already in the air, say the new person or thing, add 呢, and stop. 呢 repeats that question for the new person without saying the sentence again.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Point to This, That, or Which Thing

grammarPages.explanation: Start with 這, 那, or 哪, then add the number, measure word, and noun. With one item, 一 is often omitted; with two, use 兩. 這, 那, and 哪 mean “this,” “that,” and “which.” Use 這 when the noun is close and 那 when it is far.

subsections.title: Numerical System in Chinese
subsections.explanation: The blocks run 十 (10), 百 (100), 千 (1,000) and 萬 (10,000). Read the biggest part first, then what is left. When a middle place is empty, say 零 once; zeroes at the end are not read. In prices and amounts the last block word is often dropped (八百五 for 八百五十).

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Express a Learned Ability with 會
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what someone knows—or does not know—how to do.
grammarPages.explanation: 會 marks a skill you get through learning. Put it before the action: 我會游泳. Negate with 不會: 我不會打棒球.

teachingGlossary.meaning: shows belonging or links a describing word

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe How Well You Do an Action with 得
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe how well, fast, slowly, or how much an action is done.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 得 after a verb to describe how well you do it: 跑得很快. If there is an object, repeat the verb (跑步跑得很快) or say the object first (網球打得很好).

teachingGlossary.meaning: shows how an action is done
shows belonging or links a describing word

discoveryLab.title: Choose the lane to 得
discoveryLab.description: Every lane ends with verb + 得 + performance. The activity’s shape decides what comes before it.

choices.label: Simple verb
choices.pinyin: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài.
choices.english: He runs very fast.
choices.note: The action word 跑 goes straight before 得.

choices.label: Repeat the verb
choices.pinyin: Wǒ pǎobù pǎo de hěn kuài.
choices.english: I run very fast.
choices.note: Say the full activity 跑步, then repeat the action word 跑 before 得.

choices.label: Move object forward
choices.pinyin: Tā wǎngqiú dǎ de búcuò.
choices.english: He plays tennis quite well.
choices.note: 網球 becomes the topic, leaving 打 next to 得.

choices.label: Owned activity
choices.traditional: 他的牛肉麵做得很不錯。
choices.simplified: 他的牛肉面做得很不错。
choices.pinyin: Tā de niúròumiàn zuò de hěn búcuò.
choices.english: He cooks good beef noodles.
choices.note: 他的牛肉麵 is the topic; 做 still stands directly before 得.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Protect the core: action word + 得 + performance. Move or repeat the thing when needed.

sentenceSpine.title: Build the unbreakable core
sentenceSpine.description: Three blocks. The middle block is the rule that never changes.
notes: Right: 跑步 + 跑得 + 很快. Repeat 跑 so the action word touches 得.
Wrong: 跑步 + 得 + 很快. The word 步 cannot attach directly to 得.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say “A Little” with 有一點兒
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a small, often inconvenient degree: a little tired, cold, or small.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 有一點兒 (or 有點兒) before a describing word to say it is slightly so — usually for a small problem.

teachingGlossary.meaning: shows belonging or links a describing word

discoveryLab.title: Turn up only one notch
discoveryLab.description: The dial makes the describing word softer — often before you explain a problem or say no.
discoveryLab.prompt: What kind of small problem appears?

choices.label: Feeling
choices.traditional: 今天我有點兒忙，我不想去。
choices.simplified: 今天我有点儿忙，我不想去。
choices.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ yǒudiǎnr máng, wǒ bù xiǎng qù.
choices.english: I am a little busy today. I do not want to go.
choices.note: 有點兒忙 explains why the speaker does not want to go.

choices.label: Evaluation
choices.pinyin: Wǒ juéde yǒudiǎnr guì.
choices.english: I feel it is a little expensive.
choices.note: It is a little expensive, so you may choose another place.

choices.label: Reservation
choices.traditional: 我很喜歡這件衣服，可是我覺得有點兒小。
choices.simplified: 我很喜欢这件衣服，可是我觉得有点儿小。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhè jiàn yīfu, kěshì wǒ juéde yǒudiǎnr xiǎo.
choices.english: I like these clothes very much, but I think they are a little small.
choices.note: The clothes look nice, but they are a little small.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Say who or what first, then 有點兒, then the describing word. One small notch, often for a mild problem.

contrast.title: A little vs. a little amount
contrast.description: 有點兒 softens a describing word. 點兒 after an action or a thing means a small amount.

items.label: Small degree
items.english: The weather is a little cold.
items.note: 有點兒 comes directly before the adjective 冷.

items.label: Small amount
items.english: I want a little to drink.
items.note: 點兒 measures a small amount of 飲料.

patternRows.english: The weather is a little cold.
I am a little hungry.

items.question: Can I say 有點兒很忙 to mean “a little busy”?
items.answer: Put 有點兒 directly before 忙; do not add 很.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Ask and Give Permission with 可以
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Offer a possible solution or ask whether an action is permitted.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 可以 to ask for permission or suggest a solution. Ask with 可以…嗎 or 可不可以. Answer with 可以 to allow it, or 不可以 to say no.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 從 and 到: From and To
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say where someone comes from and where they go.
grammarPages.explanation: 從 means from. 到 means to. Put the place right after it, then end with 來 (come) or 去 (go).
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 從 / 到 + place + 來 / 去

items.question: Which place follows 從?
items.answer: Put the starting place after 從 and the destination after 到.
items.wrongTraditional: 我到學校從我家去上課。

right.traditional: 我從我家到學校去上課。
right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng wǒ jiā dào xuéxiào qù shàngkè.
right.english: I go to school from my home for class.
right.simplified: 我从我家到学校去上课。

items.question: He is coming to my home; 來 or 去?
items.answer: Use 來 because the trip ends at the speaker’s home.
items.wrongTraditional: 他從旅館到我家去吃飯。

right.traditional: 他從旅館到我家來吃飯。
right.simplified: 他从旅馆到我家来吃饭。
right.pinyin: Tā cóng lǚguǎn dào wǒ jiā lái chīfàn.
right.english: He is coming from the hotel to my home to eat.

items.question: Where does 去 go in 到他家去?
items.answer: Put 去 after 到 and the destination: 到他家去.

right.english: I went to his place.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: 了: Something Changed
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that something is new or has changed.
grammarPages.explanation: 了 at the end of a sentence means something is new: it was not true before, but it is now.

items.answer: Put 了 after 餓 to show the new state.

items.question: Where does 了 go in 可以上車了?

items.question: Can 不可以 follow the action here?
items.answer: Put 不可以 before 玩手機 to say it is no longer allowed.

text.simplified: 元真，我们明天几点去找你的韩国朋友？
text.pinyin: Yuánzhēn, wǒmen míngtiān jǐ diǎn qù zhǎo nǐ de Hánguó péngyǒu?
text.english: Yuanzhen, what time are we going to meet up with your Korean friends tomorrow?

text.simplified: 我们下午四点要到天美饭店，她在那里等我们。

text.traditional: 我們要怎麼去？坐捷運還是坐公車？
text.simplified: 我们要怎么去？坐捷运还是坐公车？
text.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zěnme qù? Zuò jiéyùn háishì zuò gōngchē?
text.english: How do we get there? By MRT or bus?

text.traditional: 聽說那家飯店不遠，我想我們可以從學校走路去。
text.simplified: 听说那家饭店不远，我想我们可以从学校走路去。
text.pinyin: Tīngshuō nà jiā fàndiàn bù yuǎn, wǒ xiǎng wǒmen kěyǐ cóng xuéxiào zǒulù qù.
text.english: I heard that the hotel is not far; I think we can go there from the school on foot.

text.traditional: 可是我不知道怎麼走，妳知道嗎？
text.simplified: 可是我不知道怎么走，你知道吗？
text.pinyin: Kěshì wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme zǒu, nǐ zhīdào ma?
text.english: But I don’t know how to get there, do you?

text.traditional: 我也不知道。我們可以先上網看地圖。
text.simplified: 我也不知道。我们可以先上网看地图。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yě bù zhīdào. Wǒmen kěyǐ xiān shàngwǎng kàn dìtú.
text.english: I don’t know either. We can check the map online first.

text.traditional: 啊！上課了！我們先上課吧。

text.pinyin: Ā! Shàngkè le! Wǒmen xiān shàngkè ba.
text.english: Ah! The class has started! Let’s go to class now.

text.traditional: 好。
text.simplified: 好。
text.pinyin: Hǎo.
text.english: Okay.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Pair Two True Qualities
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe two qualities or abilities that are true at the same time.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 又 before each of two qualities or actions describing the same subject; do not put nouns directly after 又.
grammarPages.pattern: Person or thing + 又 + quality 1 + 又 + quality 2

He can both sing and paint.

items.question: Does each quality need 又?
items.answer: Put 又 before 快 and again before 方便.

items.question: Can 又 stand before 他?

right.english: He can both sing and paint.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: 好 / 難 + Verb
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what is pleasant or easy to do.
grammarPages.explanation: 好 or 難 before a perception verb says something is pleasant or unpleasant. Before an action verb, it says something is easy or hard to do.

text.traditional: 這家餐廳的牛肉麵很好吃，我常吃。
text.simplified: 这家餐厅的牛肉面很好吃，我常吃。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de niúròu miàn hěn hǎochī, wǒ cháng chī.
text.english: The beef noodles is delicious from this restaurant; I have (it) often.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

text.traditional: 這杯茶有點兒難喝，我不要喝。
text.simplified: 这杯茶有点儿难喝，我不要喝。
text.pinyin: Zhè bēi chá yǒu diǎnr nánhē, wǒ bú yào hē.
text.english: This cup of tea tastes a bit bad; I don’t want to drink it.

text.traditional: 這件衣服的顏色很好看，我很喜歡。
text.simplified: 这件衣服的颜色很好看，我很喜欢。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de yánsè hěn hǎokàn, wǒ hěn xǐhuān.
text.english: The color of this piece of clothing is good; I like it very much.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

text.english: You sing very well. Can you do it now?

words.meaning: links an action to how well it is done

text.traditional: 這首中文歌很好唱，我朋友都會唱。
text.simplified: 这首中文歌很好唱，我朋友都会唱。
text.pinyin: Zhè shǒu Zhōngwén gē hěn hǎochàng, wǒ péngyǒu dōu huì chàng.
text.english: This Chinese song is easy to sing; all of my friends can sing it.

text.traditional: 弟弟不喜歡說英文，他覺得英文很難學。

text.english: There is only one department store in the vicinity, so it is easy to find.

text.traditional: 這輛腳踏車太小了，很難騎。
text.simplified: 这辆脚踏车太小了，很难骑。
text.pinyin: Zhè liàng jiǎotàchē tài xiǎo le, hěn nánqí.
text.english: This bike is too small; it is difficult to ride.

subsections.title: Easy or difficult
subsections.explanation: 好 or 難 describes how easy or hard the action is.

items.question: Does 好 always mean easy?
items.answer: With a perception verb, it describes something pleasant.
items.wrongTraditional: 這家餐廳的牛肉麵很吃好，我常吃。

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 跟 as a Preposition
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 跟 to do something with someone, speak to someone, or get something from someone.
grammarPages.explanation: 跟 comes before a person. It can mean “with” (do something together), “to” (speak or ask a person), or “from” (learn or borrow from a person). A helping verb or adverb goes before 跟.

items.question: I go to the hospital with my friend — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: In this pattern the subject comes first, then 跟 + the person who joins you: 我跟朋友去醫院。 A different subject can lead, as in 朋友跟我去醫院, but the 跟 phrase still comes before the action.

right.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.

items.question: I tell my friend something — where does my friend go?
items.answer: The person you tell comes right after 跟, before the action word: 我跟朋友說。

right.english: I speak to my friend.

items.question: I speak Chinese to the doctor — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: Put 跟 right before the person you speak to: 我跟醫生說中文。 The subject comes first; the 跟 phrase comes before the verb.

right.english: I speak Chinese to the doctor.

items.question: Where does 了 go with a quantity — after the verb or after the object?
items.answer: In this past-action sentence, put 了 after the verb, before the quantity: 我喝了兩杯咖啡. Without 了 before the quantity, the sentence has a different (change-of-state) meaning.

items.question: What does a second 了 add?
items.answer: One 了 reports a finished past action. The final 了 says “so far”: 我已經喝了兩杯咖啡了 means two cups so far, and more may follow.

items.question: In 是…的, does the sentence end with 了 or 的?
items.answer: Use 的 to close the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天來的. 了 is not the ending here.

items.question: Can I leave out 是 in a negative sentence?
items.answer: No. 是 cannot be left out in a negative sentence: 他不是開車來的.

right.english: He did not come by car.

items.question: Where does 的 go?
items.answer: At the end of the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天到的. Do not drop it after the verb.

items.question: Is the “then” word 再 or 在?
items.answer: 再 means “then, later” in a sequence. 在 is “at” or “happening now”: 我們晚上再去。

right.english: We will go in the evening.

items.question: What comes first: 等 or the action it waits for?
items.answer: 等 comes before the condition: 等她起床了，你再跟她說. Do not put 再 before 等.

right.traditional: 等她起床了，你再跟她說。
right.pinyin: Děng tā qǐchuáng le, nǐ zài gēn tā shuō.

items.wrongSimplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。

items.question: Where does 先 go in 先…等…再…?
items.answer: 先 comes before the first action: 你先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯.

text.traditional: 妳跟那位新朋友見面了沒有？
text.simplified: 你跟那位新朋友见面了没有？
text.pinyin: Nǐ gēn nà wèi xīn péngyǒu jiànmiàn le méiyǒu?
text.english: Have you met up with your new friend yet?

text.traditional: 我還沒決定要不要跟他見面。
text.simplified: 我还没决定要不要跟他见面。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi juédìng yào bú yào gēn tā jiànmiàn.
text.english: I haven’t decided to meet him or not.

text.traditional: 妳擔心什麼？
text.simplified: 你担心什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ dānxīn shénme?
text.english: What are you worried about?

text.traditional: 我有點兒緊張，我以前沒有這種經驗，所以覺得這樣有點兒奇怪。
text.simplified: 我有点儿紧张，我以前没有这种经验，所以觉得这样有点儿奇怪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǐqián méiyǒu zhè zhǒng jīngyàn, suǒyǐ juéde zhèyàng yǒudiǎnr qíguài.
text.english: I am a little nervous. I have never had an experience like this before, so I think it is a little strange.

text.traditional: 妳不要緊張，我有辦法，我跟妳一起去。
text.simplified: 你不要紧张，我有办法，我跟你一起去。
text.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǒu bànfǎ, wǒ gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù.
text.english: Don’t be nervous. I have an idea: I can be there for you.

text.traditional: 太好了，謝謝妳幫我的忙。
text.simplified: 太好了，谢谢你帮我的忙。
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le, xièxie nǐ bāng wǒ de máng.
text.english: Great! Thank you for helping me.

text.traditional: 不客氣。妳打算什麼時候跟他見面？
text.simplified: 不客气。你打算什么时候跟他见面？
text.pinyin: Bú kèqi. Nǐ dǎsuàn shénme shíhou gēn tā jiànmiàn?
text.english: You’re welcome. When do you plan to meet him?

text.traditional: 可能這個週末吧。如果妳有空，我再跟他約時間。
text.simplified: 可能这个周末吧。如果你有空，我再跟他约时间。
text.pinyin: Kěnéng zhège zhōumò ba. Rúguǒ nǐ yǒukòng, wǒ zài gēn tā yuē shíjiān.
text.english: Maybe this weekend. If you are free, I will arrange a time with him.

text.traditional: 有空啊，但是我明天不會來學校，等妳決定了，再給我打電話吧。
text.simplified: 有空啊，但是我明天不会来学校，等你决定了，再给我打电话吧。
text.pinyin: Yǒukòng a, dànshì wǒ míngtiān bú huì lái xuéxiào, děng nǐ juédìng le, zài gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà ba.
text.english: I am free, but I won’t come to school tomorrow. When you decide, call me.

items.question: I write letters using Chinese. Where does 中文 go?
items.answer: 中文 is the tool, so it goes right after 用, before the action: 用中文寫信.

items.question: Can you write with a brush — do I still need 用?
items.answer: Yes. 用 stays between 會 and the tool: 會用毛筆寫字. English drops the word “use”; Chinese does not.

items.question: I chat with friends in Chinese — 用 or 跟 before 中文?
items.answer: 用. 用 names the language or tool. 跟 is for the person you do it with: 跟朋友.

right.pinyin: Wǒ yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
right.english: I chat with friends in Chinese.

text.traditional: A：我覺得你中文進步了。B：真的嗎？可能是因為最近我常常用中文跟朋友聊天。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ juéde nǐ Zhōngwén jìnbù le. B: Zhēnde ma? Kěnéng shì yīnwèi zuìjìn wǒ chángcháng yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.

items.question: I go home before three. Where does 以前 go?
items.answer: Right after the time: 三點以前. 我以前三點回家 means something else — “I used to go home at three.”

right.pinyin: Wǒ sān diǎn yǐqián huí jiā.
right.english: I go home before three.

items.question: I want to be a reporter after graduating. Where does 以後 go?
items.answer: Right after the event: 畢業以後. Put it before the event and 以後畢業 means “graduate later.”

right.english: After graduating, I will become a reporter.

items.question: I want to be a reporter someday. Is 半年以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 半年以後 means “six months from now.” For a someday plan, use plain 以後.

right.english: I will become a reporter someday.

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say who you speak to, what is good or bad for something, and how someone treats another person.
grammarPages.explanation: 對 points toward a person or thing. Use it for the person you speak to, for something that is good or bad for a target, and for how someone treats another person.

items.question: The boss is kind to me. Why does 我 come so early?
items.answer: 對 points at the receiver, so 我 follows it right away: 對我好. English puts “to me” at the end; Chinese does not.

right.english: The boss is kind to me.

items.question: My coworkers are kind to me. Did I say it right with 我對同事很好?
items.answer: No — you turned the arrow around. The person right after 對 receives the kindness, so it is 同事對我很好.

right.english: My coworkers are kind to me.

items.question: Phones are bad for my eyes — 對 or 跟 before 眼睛?
items.answer: 對. 對 shows where the effect lands. 跟 is for doing something together with someone.

text.pinyin: Lǎoshī wèn wǒmen xiǎng zuò shénme gōngzuò, dàjiā dōu shuō de hěn gāoxìng.
text.english: The teacher asked us what jobs we want to do. Everybody enjoyed talking about it.

words.meaning: links an action to how it went

text.traditional: 我知道友美想當護理師。別的同學呢？
text.simplified: 我知道友美想当护理师。别的同学呢？
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào Yǒuměi xiǎng dāng hùlǐshī. Bié de tóngxué ne?
text.english: I know that Youmei wants to be a nurse. How about the others?

text.traditional: 宜文希望可以用中文和英文工作，所以她以後想當記者，元真想在銀行工作。
text.simplified: 宜文希望可以用中文和英文工作，所以她以后想当记者，元真想在银行工作。
text.pinyin: Yíwén xīwàng kěyǐ yòng Zhōngwén hé Yīngwén gōngzuò, suǒyǐ tā yǐhòu xiǎng dāng jìzhě, Yuánzhēn xiǎng zài yínháng gōngzuò.
text.english: Yiwen wants a job which requires Chinese and English language skills, so she wants to be a reporter in the future. Yuanzhen wants to work for a bank.

text.traditional: 那你畢業以後想做什麼？
text.simplified: 那你毕业以后想做什么？
text.pinyin: Nà nǐ bìyè yǐhòu xiǎng zuò shénme?
text.english: What job do you want to do after you graduate from school?

text.traditional: 我以前想當大公司的老闆，可是老闆要做的事情太多，現在覺得當醫生比較好。那你想做什麼？
text.simplified: 我以前想当大公司的老板，可是老板要做的事情太多，现在觉得当医生比较好。那你想做什么？
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián xiǎng dāng dà gōngsī de lǎobǎn, kěshì lǎobǎn yào zuò de shìqing tài duō, xiànzài juéde dāng yīshēng bǐjiào hǎo. Nà nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme?
text.english: I wanted to be a business owner, but there are so many things to do as a business owner. Now I think being a doctor is better. What do you want to do then?

text.traditional: 當醫生很不錯，但是太忙了，我只想每天可以準時上班、下班。
text.simplified: 当医生很不错，但是太忙了，我只想每天可以准时上班、下班。
text.pinyin: Dāng yīshēng hěn búcuò, dànshì tài máng le, wǒ zhǐ xiǎng měitiān kěyǐ zhǔnshí shàngbān、xiàbān.
text.english: Being a doctor is great, but doctors are too busy. I just want to clock in and clock out on time.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Mark a Life Experience with 過
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Talk about experiences you have had, and say you have already done something.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 過 right after a verb for an experience: something you have done before. V過了 relates the finished action closely to now. Use 沒 + verb + 過 for “have not.”

lessonWorld.title: Add an experience
lessonWorld.prompt: The speaker has seen this film.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我看過這部電影。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我看过这部电影。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ kànguo zhè bù diànyǐng.
lessonWorld.english: I have seen this film.

items.question: Have you ever tried stinky tofu — 吃了 or 吃過?
items.answer: 吃過. 了 asks about one finished meal. 過 asks whether it ever happened in your life.

right.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?

items.question: I have worked at a restaurant. Where does 過 go?
items.answer: Between the two parts of 上班: 上過班. It cannot sit at the end of the whole action.

right.english: I have worked at a restaurant before.

items.question: I have not been to Japan — 不 or 沒 before 去過?
items.answer: 沒. 沒 says the experience never happened. 不 says you refuse or will not do it.

right.english: I have not been to Japan.

text.traditional: 很多台灣人去過日本，因為從台灣到日本不遠。
text.pinyin: Hěnduō Táiwānrén qùguo Rìběn, yīnwèi cóng Táiwān dào Rìběn bù yuǎn.
text.english: Many Taiwanese people have been to Japan, because Japan is not far from Taiwan.
text.simplified: 很多台湾人去过日本，因为从台湾到日本不远。

text.traditional: A：他來過我們家嗎？B：來過，那個時候你不在家。
text.pinyin: A: Tā láiguo wǒmen jiā ma? B: Láiguo, nàge shíhou nǐ bú zài jiā.
text.english: A: Has he been to our home? B: Yes; you were not at home then.
text.simplified: A：他来过我们家吗？B：来过，那个时候你不在家。

text.traditional: A：你吃過臭豆腐嗎？B：我還沒吃過，聽說很特別。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ chīguo chòudòufu ma? B: Wǒ hái méi chīguo, tīngshuō hěn tèbié.
text.english: A: Have you eaten stinky tofu? B: I have not eaten it yet; I hear it is very special.
text.simplified: A：你吃过臭豆腐吗？B：我还没吃过，听说很特别。

text.traditional: A：你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？B：我吃過了，你們去吃吧！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma? B: Wǒ chīguo le, nǐmen qù chī ba!
text.english: A: Do you want to eat lunch with us? B: I have already eaten; you go eat.
text.simplified: A：你要跟我们一起吃午饭吗？B：我吃过了，你们去吃吧！

text.traditional: A：李小姐今天要來我們公司，她來過了嗎？B：她來過了，是早上來的。
text.pinyin: A: Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān yào lái wǒmen gōngsī, tā láiguo le ma? B: Tā láiguo le, shì zǎoshang lái de.
text.english: A: Miss Li is coming to our company today. Has she been here? B: She has; she came in the morning.
text.simplified: A：李小姐今天要来我们公司，她来过了吗？B：她来过了，是早上来的。

text.traditional: A：他給大家寫了一張卡片，你們都看過了嗎？B：我看過了。C：我還沒看。
text.pinyin: A: Tā gěi dàjiā xiě le yì zhāng kǎpiàn, nǐmen dōu kànguo le ma? B: Wǒ kànguo le. C: Wǒ hái méi kàn.
text.english: A: He wrote a card for everyone. Have you all seen it? B: I have. C: I have not yet.
text.simplified: A：他给大家写了一张卡片，你们都看过了吗？B：我看过了。C：我还没看。

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Open a Moment with 的時候
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what happens during a situation or activity.
grammarPages.explanation: Put the situation or activity before 的時候. Then say what happens in that moment.

lessonWorld.title: Set the moment
lessonWorld.prompt: The speaker likes going out for sport when the weather is good.
lessonWorld.traditional: 天氣好的時候，我喜歡出去運動。
lessonWorld.simplified: 天气好的时候，我喜欢出去运动。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Tiānqì hǎo de shíhou, wǒ xǐhuān chūqù yùndòng.
lessonWorld.english: When the weather is good, I like to go out for sport.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
I like to go out for sport

complement.meaning: I like to go out for sport

columns.meaning: I like to go out for sport

patternRows.english: When the weather is good, I like to go out for sport.

items.question: When working, I use Chinese — is it 工作時候 or 工作的時候?
items.answer: Keep 的. 的 connects the situation to 時候: 工作的時候.

right.english: When working, speak Chinese.

items.question: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music. Where does 不好 go?
items.answer: Keep the situation together: 心情不好, then 的時候. 的時候 needs the whole situation before it.

right.traditional: 心情不好的時候，聽音樂。
right.simplified: 心情不好的时候，听音乐。
right.pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhòu, tīng yīnyuè.
right.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.

items.question: I drink water while exercising. Is 運動以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 運動以後 means after exercising. For inside the moment, use 運動的時候.

right.pinyin: Yùndòng de shíhòu, wǒ hē shuǐ.
right.english: When exercising, I drink water.

liveSceneLab.title: Open a different life moment
liveSceneLab.description: The moment changes; 的時候 keeps the situation attached to what happens inside it.

choices.label: Feeling down

choices.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 談打工經驗 · Discussing work experience

text.traditional: 國安，你每天下課以後都要去麵包店工作，辛苦嗎？
text.simplified: 国安，你每天下课以后都要去面包店工作，辛苦吗？
text.pinyin: Guó’ān, nǐ měitiān xiàkè yǐhòu dōu yào qù miànbāodiàn gōngzuò, xīnkǔ ma?
text.english: Guoan, you work at the bakery everyday after school. Is it tiring?

text.traditional: 不辛苦。我很喜歡這個工作，因為可以學怎麼做麵包，而且同事也都對我很好。
text.simplified: 不辛苦。我很喜欢这个工作，因为可以学怎么做面包，而且同事也都对我很好。
text.pinyin: Bù xīnkǔ. Wǒ hěn xǐhuān zhège gōngzuò, yīnwèi kěyǐ xué zěnme zuò miànbāo, érqiě tóngshì yě dōu duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
text.english: It’s okay. I like this job very much because I get to learn how to make bread. Moreover, the colleagues are very nice to me as well.

text.traditional: 這樣你在學校的成績，不會有問題嗎？
text.simplified: 这样你在学校的成绩，不会有问题吗？
text.pinyin: Zhèyàng nǐ zài xuéxiào de chéngjì, bú huì yǒu wèntí ma?
text.english: Does it affect your studies?

text.traditional: 不會啊！我都先做功課，再去工作。
text.simplified: 不会啊！我都先做功课，再去工作。
text.pinyin: Bú huì a! Wǒ dōu xiān zuò gōngkè, zài qù gōngzuò.
text.english: No, it doesn’t. I always do my homework first, and then go to work.

items.question: Is 一 required in 看看 / 看一看?
items.answer: No. Both are correct. 一 adds a light “have a look” feel; the repeated verb is the main signal.

items.question: Can I add 了 after a reduplicated verb?
items.answer: No. The reduplication already softens the action; 了 does not follow it: 我看看, not 我看看了.

right.english: I take a look.

items.question: Where does 往 go?
items.answer: Before the direction: 從左往右寫. Do not put 往 after the verb.

items.question: Which comes first, 從 or 往?
items.answer: 從 marks the start and comes first: 從這裡往門口看. 往 marks the direction.

items.question: Can I use 到 instead of 往?
items.answer: 到 marks an endpoint, so 從左到右寫 is also correct. The book pattern uses 往 for the direction: 從左往右寫.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 國安給中明打電話 · Guoan calls Zhongming

text.traditional: 喂，中明，半個小時以前我寄了一封電子郵件給你，你看到了嗎？
text.simplified: 喂，中明，半个小时以前我寄了一封电子邮件给你，你看到了吗？
text.pinyin: Wèi, Zhōngmíng, bàn ge xiǎoshí yǐqián wǒ jì le yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn gěi nǐ, nǐ kàndào le ma?
text.english: Hello, Zhongming, I sent you an email half an hour ago. Have you read it?

text.traditional: 剛剛我的手機網路有點兒問題，不能看電子郵件，你寄的是什麼？
text.simplified: 刚刚我的手机网路有点儿问题，不能看电子邮件，你寄的是什么？
text.pinyin: Gānggāng wǒ de shǒujī wǎnglù yǒudiǎnr wèntí, bù néng kàn diànzǐ yóujiàn, nǐ jì de shì shénme?
text.english: The internet connection on my phone just had a little problem; I couldn’t read your email. What did you send me?

text.traditional: 博物館的網址。下禮拜六老師要帶我們去參觀，你可以先看看。
text.simplified: 博物馆的网址。下礼拜六老师要带我们去参观，你可以先看看。
text.pinyin: Bówùguǎn de wǎngzhǐ. Xià lǐbàiliù lǎoshī yào dài wǒmen qù cānguān, nǐ kěyǐ xiān kànkan.
text.english: I sent you a link for the museum website. The teacher is taking us to visit there next Saturday; you can take a look first.

text.traditional: 好。（看看手機）現在沒問題了，我看到了。
text.simplified: 好。（看看手机）现在没问题了，我看到了。
text.pinyin: Hǎo. (Kànkan shǒujī) Xiànzài méi wèntí le, wǒ kàndào le.
text.english: OK. (Take a look at the phone) There’s no problem now, I’ve read your email.

text.traditional: 網站上有地址，那個地方在我家附近，從我家出去，往右轉，差不多五分鐘就到了。
text.simplified: 网站上有地址，那个地方在我家附近，从我家出去，往右转，差不多五分钟就到了。
text.pinyin: Wǎngzhàn shang yǒu dìzhǐ, nà ge dìfang zài wǒ jiā fùjìn, cóng wǒ jiā chūqù, wǎng yòu zhuǎn, chàbuduō wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
text.english: There’s the address on the website; that place is close to my house. If you go from my place, you make a right turn, and you’ll be there in just about five minutes.

text.traditional: 我們應該幾點到？
text.simplified: 我们应该几点到？
text.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi jǐ diǎn dào?
text.english: What time should we be there?

text.traditional: 早上九點在博物館門口見，要記得準時到。
text.simplified: 早上九点在博物馆门口见，要记得准时到。
text.pinyin: Zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn zài bówùguǎn ménkǒu jiàn, yào jìde zhǔnshí dào.
text.english: 9 a.m. at the museum gate. Remember to get there on time.

text.traditional: 我們上個星期六去運動的時候，我到得太晚，真不好意思。下個星期我一定會準時。
text.simplified: 我们上个星期六去运动的时候，我到得太晚，真不好意思。下个星期我一定会准时。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen shàng ge xīngqīliù qù yùndòng de shíhòu, wǒ dào de tài wǎn, zhēn bù hǎoyìsi. Xià ge xīngqī wǒ yídìng huì zhǔnshí.
text.english: I am sorry for being late when we went exercising last Saturday. I’ll definitely be on time next week.

grammarPages.explanation: Put 就要 before the event and 了 at the end. A time word usually comes before 就要: 我下個月就要回國了.

items.question: Does 就要…了 need the final 了?
items.answer: The book’s pattern closes with 了: 他明天就要來了. Without 了 the sentence sounds unfinished in this context.

right.pinyin: Tā míngtiān jiù yào lái le.
right.english: He is coming tomorrow.

items.question: Where does 就要 go?
items.answer: Before the event: 圖書館就要關了. A time word goes before 就要.

right.english: The library is about to close.

items.question: Is 快要 also correct?
items.answer: Yes. 快要…了 is another common form. The book uses 就要 in this table; both mean “about to”.

right.pinyin: Tā míngtiān jiù yào lái le.

text.english: The movie is about to start; why has he not come yet?

text.traditional: 圖書館就要關了，你現在去也許太晚了。
text.simplified: 图书馆就要关了，你现在去也许太晚了。
text.pinyin: Túshūguǎn jiù yào guān le, nǐ xiànzài qù yěxǔ tài wǎn le.
text.english: The library is about to close; going now might be too late.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Measure an Action’s Duration
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how long an action lasts.
grammarPages.explanation: Put the duration after the verb. If the verb has an object, repeat the verb before the duration, or use V + duration + 的 + object.

lessonWorld.prompt: The group waits ten minutes and visits for three hours.

lessonWorld.simplified: 我们排队排十分钟，参观三个小时。

lessonWorld.english: We wait in line for ten minutes and visit for three hours.

grammarPages.pattern: Action + duration / Verb + object + verb + duration

items.question: Where does the duration go?
items.answer: After the verb: 我每天工作八個小時. Do not put it before the verb.

right.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
right.english: I work eight hours every day.

items.question: What happens when there is an object?
items.answer: Repeat the verb before the duration: 我每天跑步跑三十分鐘.
items.wrongTraditional: 我每天跑步三十分鐘跑。

right.traditional: 我每天跑步跑三十分鐘。
right.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān pǎobù pǎo sānshí fēnzhōng.
right.english: I run thirty minutes every day.
right.simplified: 我每天跑步跑三十分钟。

items.wrongSimplified: 我每天跑步跑三十分钟。

items.question: What does 的 do in 睡七個小時的覺?
items.answer: It joins the duration to the object: seven hours of sleep. Without 的, repeat the verb instead.

text.english: A: I have to drive for six hours tomorrow; I want to sleep first. B: Driving for six hours will surely be tiring; go to sleep.

text.traditional: A：我弟弟很愛玩手機，每天差不多玩五個小時。B：玩五個小時的手機！時間太長了！

text.traditional: 博物館五分鐘以後就要開門了，大家都到了吧？
text.simplified: 博物馆五分钟以后就要开门了，大家都到了吧？
text.pinyin: Bówùguǎn wǔ fēnzhōng yǐhòu jiù yào kāimén le, dàjiā dōu dào le ba?
text.english: The museum will be open after five minutes. Is everyone here already?

text.traditional: 中明說他快要到了。
text.simplified: 中明说他快要到了。
text.pinyin: Zhōngmíng shuō tā kuài yào dào le.
text.english: Zhongming said he’ll be here soon.

text.traditional: 老師，我們要不要先去排隊買票？
text.simplified: 老师，我们要不要先去排队买票？
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒmen yào bu yào xiān qù páiduì mǎi piào?
text.english: Teacher, should we get in line to buy tickets first?

text.traditional: 差不多需要排十分鐘的隊，那好吧，我們先去排隊。
text.simplified: 差不多需要排十分钟的队，那好吧，我们先去排队。
text.pinyin: Chàbuduō xūyào pái shí fēnzhōng de duì, nà hǎo ba, wǒmen xiān qù páiduì.
text.english: It takes about ten minutes to line up. Alright, let’s get in line to buy tickets first.

text.traditional: 今天我們打算參觀三個小時，會有人給我們介紹。進去以後，記得要安靜，不可以說話說得太大聲。
text.simplified: 今天我们打算参观三个小时，会有人给我们介绍。进去以后，记得要安静，不可以说话说得太大声。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen dǎsuàn cānguān sān ge xiǎoshí, huì yǒu rén gěi wǒmen jièshào. Jìnqù yǐhòu, jìde yào ānjìng, bù kěyǐ shuōhuà shuō de tài dàshēng.
text.english: We plan to visit for three hours today. There will be someone introducing the museum for us. After you enter, remember to keep quiet. You can’t speak loudly.

text.traditional: 老師，我剛剛先用手機上網看了很多有趣的圖片，真想馬上就看到博物館裡的東西。
text.simplified: 老师，我刚刚先用手机上网看了很多有趣的图片，真想马上就看到博物馆里的东西。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ gānggāng xiān yòng shǒujī shàngwǎng kàn le hěn duō yǒuqù de túpiàn, zhēn xiǎng mǎshàng jiù kàndào bówùguǎn lǐ de dōngxi.
text.english: Teacher, I just used my cell phone to look for some information on the internet, and I saw many interesting pictures. I want to see what they have in the museum right away.

text.traditional: 我知道你非常喜歡歷史，我想你今天一定會很開心。
text.simplified: 我知道你非常喜欢历史，我想你今天一定会很开心。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào nǐ fēicháng xǐhuān lìshǐ, wǒ xiǎng nǐ jīntiān yídìng huì hěn kāixīn.
text.english: I know you like history very much. I think you’ll enjoy it a lot today.

text.traditional: 我也在網路上找了很多文章，那些介紹和故事都非常有趣。
text.simplified: 我也在网路上找了很多文章，那些介绍和故事都非常有趣。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yě zài wǎnglù shang zhǎo le hěn duō wénzhāng, nàxiē jièshào hé gùshi dōu fēicháng yǒuqù.
text.english: I also found many articles on the internet. Those introductions and stories are very fascinating.

text.traditional: 那如果大家有問題就可以問你了。
text.simplified: 那如果大家有问题就可以问你了。
text.pinyin: Nà rúguǒ dàjiā yǒu wèntí jiù kěyǐ wèn nǐ le.
text.english: If anyone has questions, they can ask you then.

text.traditional: 要是我知道，一定會告訴大家！
text.simplified: 要是我知道，一定会告诉大家！
text.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ zhīdào, yídìng huì gàosu dàjiā!
text.english: If I know the answers, I’ll tell them for sure!

text.traditional: （往前看）中明來了！
text.simplified: （往前看）中明来了！
text.pinyin: (Wǎng qián kàn) Zhōngmíng lái le!
text.english: (Look forward) Here comes Zhongming!

text.traditional: 好，我們進去參觀吧。
text.simplified: 好，我们进去参观吧。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒmen jìnqù cānguān ba.
text.english: Okay! Let’s get in to visit.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Two Sides with 比
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Compare two people or things and say which has more of a quality.
grammarPages.explanation: Put A before 比 and B after it. Add the adjective or result after 比 + B. 多了／得多 stresses a big difference; 一點兒 means a small difference.

items.title: Grammar 1 · Compare with 跟…(不)一樣

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Things with 跟…(不)一樣
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say two people or things are the same or different.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 跟 between the two things and 一樣 for “the same”. Add 不 before 一樣 for “different”. A describing word can follow 一樣.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: A + 跟 + B + (不)一樣 (+ Describing word)

items.question: Can I compare two things with 一樣 without 跟?
items.answer: No. When you mention the second item, use 跟 before it: 越南的生肖跟中國的不一樣.
items.wrongTraditional: 越南的生肖中國的不一樣。

right.traditional: 越南的生肖跟中國的不一樣。
right.pinyin: Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de bù yíyàng.
right.english: Vietnam’s zodiac is not the same as China’s.
right.simplified: 越南的生肖跟中国的不一样。

items.wrongSimplified: 越南的生肖跟中国的不一样。

items.question: What changes 一樣 to 不一樣?
items.answer: Put 不 before 一樣 for “not the same”: 弟弟跟哥哥不一樣聰明. 弟弟跟哥哥一樣不聰明 means both are not smart — a different meaning.
items.wrongTraditional: 弟弟跟哥哥一樣不聰明。

right.traditional: 弟弟跟哥哥不一樣聰明。
right.pinyin: Dìdi gēn gēge bù yíyàng cōngmíng.
right.english: The younger brother is not as smart as the older brother.
right.simplified: 弟弟跟哥哥不一样聪明。

items.wrongSimplified: 弟弟跟哥哥不一样聪明。

items.question: Where does 得 go in the B pattern?
items.answer: Either side can carry 得, but only one: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一樣好 or 他唱歌跟哥哥唱得一樣好. Do not put 得 after both.
items.wrongTraditional: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥唱得一樣好。

right.traditional: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一樣好。
right.pinyin: Tā chànggē chàng de gēn gēge yíyàng hǎo.
right.english: He sings as well as his older brother.
right.simplified: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一样好。

items.wrongSimplified: 他唱歌唱得跟哥哥一样好。

text.traditional: 這種藥跟那種藥一樣嗎？
text.simplified: 这种药跟那种药一样吗？
text.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào gēn nà zhǒng yào yíyàng ma?
text.english: Is this medicine the same as that medicine?

text.traditional: 這件事情跟那件事情一樣重要。
text.simplified: 这件事情跟那件事情一样重要。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shìqíng gēn nà jiàn shìqíng yíyàng zhòngyào.
text.english: This matter is as important as that matter.

text.simplified: 这栋大楼的电梯跟那栋大楼的（电梯）不一样大。
text.pinyin: Zhè dòng dàlóu de diàntī gēn nà dòng dàlóu de (diàntī) bù yíyàng dà.

text.simplified: 他打球，跟哥哥打得一样好。
text.pinyin: Tā dǎqiú, gēn gēge dǎ de yíyàng hǎo.
text.english: He plays ball as well as his older brother.

text.english: What animals are there?

text.traditional: 我記得有羊、馬、兔子，最特別的是龍。你看看！
text.simplified: 我记得有羊、马、兔子，最特别的是龙。你看看！
text.pinyin: Wǒ jìdé yǒu yáng, mǎ, tùzi, zuì tèbié de shì lóng. Nǐ kànkan!
text.english: I remember there are goats, horses, rabbits, and the most special one is the dragon. Take a look!

text.traditional: 原來是十二生肖，真的很有意思。
text.simplified: 原来是十二生肖，真的很有意思。
text.pinyin: Yuánlái shì shí'èr shēngxiào, zhēn de hěn yǒuyìsi.
text.english: Oh, so it’s the Chinese zodiac! That’s really fascinating.

text.traditional: 什麼是十二生肖？
text.simplified: 什么是十二生肖？
text.pinyin: Shénme shì shí'èr shēngxiào?
text.english: What is the Chinese zodiac?

text.traditional: 華人用不一樣的動物代表每一年，一共有十二種動物。
text.simplified: 华人用不一样的动物代表每一年，一共有十二种动物。
text.pinyin: Huárén yòng bù yíyàng de dòngwù dàibiǎo měi yì nián, yígòng yǒu shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù.
text.english: Chinese people use different animals to represent each year. There are twelve animals in total.

text.traditional: 越南也有十二生肖，可是我們沒有兔年，有貓年。我是貓年出生的，屬貓。
text.simplified: 越南也有十二生肖，可是我们没有兔年，有猫年。我是猫年出生的，属猫。
text.pinyin: Yuènán yě yǒu shí'èr shēngxiào, kěshì wǒmen méiyǒu tùnián, yǒu māonián. Wǒ shì māonián chūshēng de, shǔ māo.
text.english: Vietnam also has the twelve zodiac animals, but we don't have the Year of the Rabbit; we have the Year of the Cat. I was born in the Year of the Cat, so my zodiac sign is the cat.

text.traditional: 真的？好有趣！原來越南的生肖跟中國的有點不一樣。我好想知道我屬什麼。
text.simplified: 真的？好有趣！原来越南的生肖跟中国的有点不一样。我好想知道我属什么。
text.pinyin: Zhēn de? Hǎo yǒuqù! Yuánlái Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de yǒudiǎn bù yíyàng. Wǒ hǎo xiǎng zhīdào wǒ shǔ shénme.
text.english: Really? How interesting! It turns out Vietnam's zodiac is a bit different from China's. I really want to know what sign I am.

text.traditional: 很簡單，上網一查就知道了。
text.simplified: 很简单，上网一查就知道了。
text.pinyin: Hěn jiǎndān, shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
text.english: It's very simple. Just look it up online and you'll know immediately.

text.traditional: 好，我上網查查看。
text.simplified: 好，我上网查查看。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ shàngwǎng cháchá kàn.
text.english: Okay, I'll search for it online.

items.title: Grammar 2 · Describe Ongoing States with 著

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe an Ongoing State with 著
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a continuing state or a posture.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 著 directly after a verb to show that the action or state continues: 她看著窗戶外面. The object follows 著.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

items.question: Where does 著 go?
items.answer: Directly after the verb, before the object: 她看著窗戶外面. Do not put it after the object.

right.english: She is looking outside the window.

items.question: Does 著 mean the action is finished?
items.answer: No. 著 shows a continuing state; 了 shows a completed action. 她看著窗外 is ongoing; 她看了窗外 is completed.

right.english: She is looking outside the window.

items.question: Can an object follow 著?
items.answer: Yes. Put the object after 著: 他拿著燈籠. 著 stays attached to the verb.

right.english: He is holding a lantern.

text.traditional: 他看著窗戶外面，想著他的女朋友。
text.simplified: 他看着窗户外面，想着他的女朋友。
text.pinyin: Tā kàn zhe chuānghu wàimiàn, xiǎng zhe tā de nǚpéngyǒu.
text.english: He is looking outside the window, thinking of his girlfriend.

text.traditional: 他在門口等著你，你快去找他吧。
text.simplified: 他在门口等着你，你快去找他吧。
text.pinyin: Tā zài ménkǒu děng zhe nǐ, nǐ kuài qù zhǎo tā ba.
text.english: He is waiting for you at the door; go find him quickly.

text.traditional: 很多人在那裡唱著歌、跳著舞，大家都很開心。
text.simplified: 很多人在那里唱着歌、跳着舞，大家都很开心。
text.pinyin: Hěn duō rén zài nàlǐ chàng zhe gē, tiào zhe wǔ, dàjiā dōu hěn kāixīn.
text.english: Many people are singing and dancing there; everyone is happy.

text.traditional: 大家聽著，明天一定要準時到。
text.simplified: 大家听着，明天一定要准时到。
text.pinyin: Dàjiā tīng zhe, míngtiān yídìng yào zhǔnshí dào.
text.english: Everyone listen; tomorrow you must arrive on time.

examples.teachingNote: Printed as 1 in part B.

text.traditional: 你看著我，剛才你說的是真的嗎？
text.simplified: 你看着我，刚才你说的是真的吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ kàn zhe wǒ, gāngcái nǐ shuō de shì zhēn de ma?
text.english: Look at me; is what you just said true?

examples.teachingNote: Printed as 2 in part B.

text.traditional: 你在這裡等著，他們馬上就來了。
text.simplified: 你在这里等着，他们马上就来了。
text.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhèlǐ děng zhe, tāmen mǎshàng jiù lái le.
text.english: Wait here; they are coming right away.

dialogue.title: 十二生肖 · The Chinese Animal Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 對話二 · Dialogue 2

text.traditional: 中明，你手裡拿著什麼？
text.simplified: 中明，你手里拿着什么？
text.pinyin: Zhōngmíng, nǐ shǒulǐ názhe shénme?
text.english: Zhongming, what are you holding in your hand?

text.traditional: 這是燈籠。
text.simplified: 这是灯笼。
text.pinyin: Zhè shì dēnglóng.
text.english: This is a lantern.

text.traditional: 燈籠上的小老虎好可愛。
text.simplified: 灯笼上的小老虎好可爱。
text.pinyin: Dēnglóng shàng de xiǎo lǎohǔ hǎo kě'ài.
text.english: The little tiger on the lantern is so cute.

text.traditional: 這是我朋友做的，因為他屬虎。你知道十二生肖嗎？
text.simplified: 这是我朋友做的，因为他属虎。你知道十二生肖吗？
text.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ péngyǒu zuò de, yīnwèi tā shǔ hǔ. Nǐ zhīdào shí'èr shēngxiào ma?
text.english: A friend of mine made it because he was born in the year of the tiger. Do you know about the twelve zodiac animals?

text.traditional: 知道，友美跟我講過。
text.simplified: 知道，友美跟我讲过。
text.pinyin: Zhīdào, Yǒuměi gēn wǒ jiǎng guò.
text.english: Yes, Youmei mentioned it to me.

text.traditional: 這個星期六是元宵節，你跟友美會去看燈會嗎？
text.simplified: 这个星期六是元宵节，你跟友美会去看灯会吗？
text.pinyin: Zhège xīngqíliù shì Yuánxiāojié, nǐ gēn Yǒuměi huì qù kàn dēnghuì ma?
text.english: This Saturday is the Lantern Festival. Are you and Youmei going to see the lantern show?

text.traditional: 友美說她想去，我還沒決定去不去。燈會好玩嗎？
text.simplified: 友美说她想去，我还没决定去不去。灯会好玩吗？
text.pinyin: Yǒuměi shuō tā xiǎng qù, wǒ hái méi juédìng qù bú qù. Dēnghuì hǎowán ma?
text.english: Youmei said she wants to go, but I haven't decided yet. Is the lantern festival fun?

text.traditional: 我去年去看了，很多大人帶著小孩去看燈會，非常熱鬧。我照了很多相片。
text.simplified: 我去年去看了，很多大人带着小孩去看灯会，非常热闹。我照了很多相片。
text.pinyin: Wǒ qùnián qù kàn le, hěn duō dàrén dàizhe xiǎohái qù kàn dēnghuì, fēicháng rènào. Wǒ zhào le hěn duō xiàngpiàn.
text.english: I went last year. Many adults brought their kids to see the lantern show; it was very lively. I took a lot of pictures.

text.traditional: 那我這個週末一定要去看看。
text.simplified: 那我这个周末一定要去看看。
text.pinyin: Nà wǒ zhège zhōumò yídìng yào qù kànkan.
text.english: Then I must definitely go see it this weekend.

text.traditional: 我週末還要工作，打算一下班就去看燈會。我們可以約友美一起去。
text.simplified: 我周末还要工作，打算一下班就去看灯会。我们可以约友美一起去。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò hái yào gōngzuò, dǎsuàn yí xiàbān jiù qù kàn dēnghuì. Wǒmen kěyǐ yuē Yǒuměi yìqǐ qù.
text.english: I have to work this weekend, but I plan to go see the lantern show right after getting off work. We can invite Youmei to join us.

items.title: Grammar 3 · Immediate Sequence with 一……就……

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Express Immediate Sequence with 一……就……
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one action happens right after another.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 一 before the first action and 就 before the second: 我一看書，就想睡覺. If the subjects are the same, the second subject is often omitted.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Subject 1 + 一 + Action 1，Subject 2 + 就 + Action 2

patternRows.english: Whenever he has a question, he asks the teacher.
As soon as you said it, I understood it.

items.question: Does the pattern need both 一 and 就?
items.answer: For the “as soon as” meaning, use both: 上網一查就知道了. Without 一 the sentence can still be grammatical, but it loses the immediate-sequence meaning.

right.pinyin: Shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
right.english: As soon as you look it up online, you will know.

items.question: Where does 就 go when the second subject is named?
items.answer: After the second subject: 我一說話，他就不高興. Do not put 就 before 他.

right.pinyin: Wǒ yì shuōhuà, tā jiù bù gāoxìng.
right.english: As soon as I speak, he is unhappy.

text.traditional: 我一看書，就想睡覺。
text.simplified: 我一看书，就想睡觉。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yí kànshū, jiù xiǎng shuìjiào.
text.english: As soon as I read, I feel sleepy.

text.traditional: 媽媽一知道我發燒了，就開始擔心。
text.simplified: 妈妈一知道我发烧了，就开始担心。
text.pinyin: Māma yì zhīdào wǒ fāshāo le, jiù kāishǐ dānxīn.
text.english: As soon as Mom knew I had a fever, she began to worry.

text.traditional: 他今天很奇怪，我一說話，他就不高興。
text.simplified: 他今天很奇怪，我一说话，他就不高兴。
text.pinyin: Tā jīntiān hěn qíguài, wǒ yì shuōhuà, tā jiù bù gāoxìng.
text.english: He is strange today; as soon as I speak, he is unhappy.

dialogue.title: 有趣的十二生肖 · The Interesting Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 短文 · Reading

text.traditional: 今天一進教室，就看到桌上放著幾隻用紙做的動物，黑板上也有很多張動物的圖片，我覺得很有趣。
text.simplified: 今天一进教室，就看到桌上放着几只用纸做的动物，黑板上也有很多张动物的图片，我觉得很有趣。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān yí jìn jiàoshì, jiù kàndào zhuō shàng fàngzhe jǐ zhī yòng zhǐ zuò de dòngwù, hēibǎn shàng yě yǒu hěn duō zhāng dòngwù de túpiàn, wǒ juéde hěn yǒuqù.
text.english: As soon as I walked into the classroom today, I saw several paper animals placed on the table, and there were also many pictures of animals on the blackboard. I found it very interesting.

text.traditional: 老師告訴我們，很久以前，有十二種動物一起參加了一個過河比賽，看誰游得最快。
text.simplified: 老师告诉我们，很久以前，有十二种动物一起参加了一个过河比赛，看谁游得最快。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī gàosu wǒmen, hěn jiǔ yǐqián, yǒu shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù yìqǐ cānjiā le yí ge guòhé bǐsài, kàn shéi yóu de zuì kuài.
text.english: The teacher told us that a long time ago, twelve animals entered a river-crossing race together to see who could swim the fastest.

text.traditional: 開始比賽以後，每隻動物都游得很快很辛苦。老鼠先過了河，第二個到的是牛，最後到的是豬。老鼠贏了，排第一，其他動物排後面。
text.simplified: 开始比赛以后，每只动物都游得很快很辛苦。老鼠先过了河，第二个到的是牛，最后到的是猪。老鼠赢了，排第一，其他动物排后面。
text.pinyin: Kāishǐ bǐsài yǐhòu, měi zhī dòngwù dōu yóu de hěn kuài hěn xīnkǔ. Lǎoshǔ xiān guò le hé, dì èr ge dào de shì niú, zuìhòu dào de shì zhū. Lǎoshǔ yíng le, pái dì yī, qítā dòngwù pái hòumiàn.
text.english: After the race began, each animal swam hard and fast. The rat crossed the river first, the ox arrived second, and the pig arrived last. The rat won, ranking first, and the other animals lined up behind.

text.traditional: 這次比賽以後，華人就用鼠、牛、虎、兔、龍、蛇、馬、羊、猴、雞、狗和豬代表每一年，而且叫這十二種動物「十二生肖」。
text.simplified: 这次比赛以后，华人就用鼠、牛、虎、兔、龙、蛇、马、羊、猴、鸡、狗和猪代表每一年，而且叫这十二种动物「十二生肖」。
text.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài yǐhòu, Huárén jiù yòng shǔ, niú, hǔ, tù, lóng, shé, mǎ, yáng, hóu, jī, gǒu hé zhū dàibiǎo měi yì nián, érqiě jiào zhè shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù "shí'èr shēngxiào".
text.english: After this race, Chinese people used the rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog, and pig to represent each year, calling these twelve animals the "Twelve Zodiac Animals".

text.traditional: 華人聊天的時候，會問別人「你屬什麼？」。每年到了元宵節，代表那年的動物燈籠，也會最受歡迎。
text.simplified: 华人聊天的时候，会问别人「你属什么？」。每年到了元宵节，代表那年的动物灯笼，也会最受欢迎。
text.pinyin: Huárén liáotiān de shíhòu, huì wèn biérén "nǐ shǔ shénme?". Měi nián dào le Yuánxiāojié, dàibiǎo nà nián de dòngwù dēnglóng, yě huì zuì shòu huānyíng.
text.english: When chatting, Chinese people often ask others, "What is your zodiac sign?". Every year during the Lantern Festival, the lantern representing the animal of that year is also the most popular.

items.title: Grammar 1 · Distances with 離

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say How Close or Far Two Places Are with 離
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how far one place is from another.
grammarPages.explanation: 離 means “from” in a distance phrase. Put the first place before 離, the second place after it, then an adverb and 遠 (far) or 近 (close).

teachingGlossary.pinyin: zuò sān ge xiǎoshí de fēijī

grammarPages.pattern: Place A + 離 + Place B + Adverb + 遠／近

patternRows.english: My home is very far from the company.
Japan is really close to Taiwan.
The bank is not too far from here.

items.question: Can I say how far two places are without 離?
items.answer: No. 離 is the word that names the distance. Without it, the sentence does not compare two places.

right.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
right.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
right.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

items.question: What is the difference between 離 and 從?
items.answer: 離 tells a distance between two places. 從 tells where a trip starts. Use 離 for distance.

right.english: The school is far from the hospital.

items.question: Where does 很近 go in the sentence?
items.answer: Right after the second place. The pattern is Place A 離 Place B 很近.
items.wrongTraditional: 離火車站百貨公司很近。
items.wrongSimplified: 离火车站百货公司很近。

right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

dialogue.title: 在台灣旅行 · Traveling in Taiwan
dialogue.setting: 對話一 · Dialogue 1

text.traditional: 國安，這次學校放假，你有什麼計畫？
text.simplified: 国安，这次学校放假，你有什么计划？
text.pinyin: Guó'ān, zhè cì xuéxiào fàngjià, nǐ yǒu shénme jìhuà?
text.english: Guo'an, school is going on vacation this time. Do you have any plans?

text.traditional: 我還沒打算要做什麼。這次放假，沒有上次放得那麼久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪裡比較好。
text.simplified: 我还没打算要做什么。这次放假，没有上次放得那么久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪里比较好。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi dǎsuàn yào zuò shénme. Zhè cì fàngjià, méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ, zhǐ fàng sān tiān jià, wǒ bù zhīdào qù nǎlǐ bǐjiào hǎo.
text.english: I haven't decided what to do yet. This break is not as long as the last one—only three days—so I don't know where it's best to go.

text.traditional: 我覺得太魯閣不錯，有山又有河。
text.simplified: 我觉得太鲁阁不错，有山又有河。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde Tàilǔgé búcuò, yǒu shān yòu yǒu hé.
text.english: I think Taroko Gorge is great; it has both mountains and rivers.

text.traditional: 在哪裡？離台北遠不遠？
text.simplified: 在哪里？离台北远不远？
text.pinyin: Zài nǎlǐ? Lí Táiběi yuǎn bù yuǎn?
text.english: Where is it? Is it far from Taipei?

text.traditional: 在花蓮。花蓮在台灣東部，離台北有點遠，你可以坐火車去，也可以開車去，差不多四個小時。
text.simplified: 在花莲。花莲在台湾东部，离台北有点远，你可以坐火车去，也可以开车去，差不多四个小时。
text.pinyin: Zài Huālián. Huālián zài Táiwān dōngbù, lí Táiběi yǒudiǎn yuǎn, nǐ kěyǐ zuò huǒchē qù, yě kěyǐ kāichē qù, chàbùduō sì ge xiǎoshí.
text.english: It's in Hualien. Hualien is in eastern Taiwan, somewhat far from Taipei. You can take a train or drive there; it takes about four hours.

text.traditional: 你去過嗎？
text.simplified: 你去过吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ qù guò ma?
text.english: Have you been there?

text.traditional: 我小學六年級的時候去過，我很喜歡那裡。
text.simplified: 我小学六年级的时候去过，我很喜欢那里。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoxué liù niánjí de shíhòu qù guò, wǒ hěn xǐhuān nàlǐ.
text.english: I went when I was in sixth grade of elementary school. I liked it very much.

text.traditional: 那你打算去哪裡玩？
text.simplified: 那你打算去哪里玩？
text.pinyin: Nà nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎlǐ wán?
text.english: Where do you plan to go for fun?

text.traditional: 我想去合歡山。報紙上寫，這幾天可能會下雪。
text.simplified: 我想去合欢山。报纸上写，这几天可能会下雪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Héhuān Shān. Bàozhǐ shàng xiě, zhè jǐ tiān kěnéng huì xiàxuě.
text.english: I want to go to Hehuanshan. The newspaper says it might snow these few days.

text.traditional: 下雪？我還沒看過雪，合歡山在哪裡？
text.simplified: 下雪？我还没看过雪，合欢山在哪里？
text.pinyin: Xiàxuě? Wǒ hái méi kàn guò xuě, Héhuān Shān zài nǎlǐ?
text.english: Snow? I haven't seen snow before. Where is Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 在台灣的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.simplified: 在台湾的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān de zhōngbù, Rìyuè Tán yě zài fùjìn.
text.english: In central Taiwan. Sun Moon Lake is also nearby.

text.traditional: 日月潭很有名，我在書上看過，離合歡山近嗎？
text.simplified: 日月潭很有名，我在书上看过，离合欢山近吗？
text.pinyin: Rìyuè Tán hěn yǒumíng, wǒ zài shū shàng kàn guò, lí Héhuān Shān jìn ma?
text.english: Sun Moon Lake is very famous. I read about it in a book. Is it close to Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 不遠，我想去玩三天兩夜，先去日月潭，再去合歡山。
text.simplified: 不远，我想去玩三天两夜，先去日月潭，再去合欢山。
text.pinyin: Bù yuǎn, wǒ xiǎng qù wán sān tiān liǎng yè, xiān qù Rìyuè Tán, zài qù Héhuān Shān.
text.english: Not far. I want to go for three days and two nights: go to Sun Moon Lake first, and then to Hehuanshan.

text.traditional: 你記得多照一些相片給我看！
text.simplified: 你记得多照一些相片给我看！
text.pinyin: Nǐ jìdé duō zhào yìxiē xiàngpiàn gěi wǒ kàn!
text.english: Remember to take more pictures for me to see!

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say What Changed from Before with 本來 (原來) … 後來 …
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say an original plan or state and what changed later.
grammarPages.explanation: 本來 or 原來 introduces the original plan or state. 後來 introduces the change or what actually happened.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
originally wanted to go to Taroko

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 本來／原來 + Original state + 後來 + Result

items.question: Do 本來 and 原來 mean the same thing?
items.answer: Yes, for showing how things were at first. Use either one at the start of the changed story.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。

right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I keep 來 or 了 at the very end?
items.answer: The changed part ends with 了. 後來 sits before the changed part, not at the end.
items.wrongTraditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車來。
items.wrongSimplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车来。

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Can I use only 後來 to show a change?
items.answer: A change story reads better with both parts. 本來 (or 原來) starts it, and 後來 gives the change.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

text.traditional: 昨天本來天氣很好，後來下雨了。
text.simplified: 昨天本来天气很好，后来下雨了。
text.pinyin: Zuótiān běnlái tiānqì hěn hǎo, hòulái xià yǔ le.
text.english: Yesterday the weather was nice at first, then it rained.

examples.teachingNote: 本來 starts the first plan; 後來 gives what changed.

text.traditional: 我今天本來想去看電影，後來下雨就沒去了。
text.simplified: 我今天本来想去看电影，后来下雨就没去了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān běnlái xiǎng qù kàn diànyǐng, hòulái xià yǔ jiù méi qù le.
text.english: I first wanted to see a movie today, but then it rained so I did not go.

text.traditional: 他本來不會說中文，後來在台灣學了一年，現在說得很好。

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Two Things as Even More with 更
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one thing has even more of a quality than another.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 更 before the adjective to raise the degree: A 比 B 更 + adjective.
grammarPages.pattern: A + 比 + B + 更 + Adjective

patternRows.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.
My older brother’s grades are even better than mine.
Kaohsiung’s weather is even warmer than Taipei’s.

items.question: Can I compare with only 更?
items.answer: For a two-thing comparison you also need 比. The shape is thing 比 thing 更 + describing word.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Where does 更 go?
items.answer: Right before the describing word. It is not after the second thing.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Does 更 mean the most?
items.answer: No. 更 means even more between two things. Say 最 for the most among a group.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

text.traditional: A：你的成績比你弟弟好嗎？ B：對，可是我哥哥的成績比我更好。
text.simplified: A：你的成绩比你弟弟好吗？ B：对，可是我哥哥的成绩比我更好。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ de chéngjī bǐ nǐ dìdi hǎo ma? B: Duì, kěshì wǒ gēge de chéngjī bǐ wǒ gèng hǎo.
text.english: A: Are your grades better than your younger brother’s? B: Yes, but my older brother’s grades are even better than mine.

text.traditional: 今年的表演比去年的更有意思，我覺得你應該來看。
text.simplified: 今年的表演比去年的更有意思，我觉得你应该来看。
text.pinyin: Jīnnián de biǎoyǎn bǐ qùnián de gèng yǒu yìsi, wǒ juéde nǐ yīnggāi lái kàn.
text.english: This year’s performance is even more interesting than last year’s; I think you should come see it.

text.traditional: 我覺得家人和朋友都很重要，但家人比朋友更重要。
text.simplified: 我觉得家人和朋友都很重要，但家人比朋友更重要。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde jiārén hé péngyǒu dōu hěn zhòngyào, dàn jiārén bǐ péngyǒu gèng zhòngyào.
text.english: I think family and friends are both important, but family is even more important than friends.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Link Two Finished Actions with 就
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one finished action is followed immediately by another.
grammarPages.explanation: Finish the first action with 了, then use 就 before the next action. The second action follows right away.

teachingGlossary.pinyin: měitiān wǎnshang wǒ xǐ le zǎo
teachingGlossary.meaning: every night I take a shower
ending word: something is done or has changed

grammarPages.pattern: First action + 了 + 就 + Next action

items.question: Do I need 就 between the two actions?
items.answer: Yes. 就 is the word that links the finished action to what happened right after.

items.question: Do both actions need 了?

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe How an Action Turned Out with 得
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe how an action was done or how it turned out.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 得 directly after the verb, then the state complement that describes the action.

teachingGlossary.pinyin: zhè zhāng zhàopiàn lǐ de rén

He introduced his country extremely well.

items.question: When do I use 的 vs 得?
items.answer: Use 的 to describe a noun (漂亮的風景). Use 得 right after an action verb to describe how it is done (玩得很開心).

right.english: I had a great time.

items.question: Where does 得 go if the verb has an object?
items.answer: Either repeat the verb (放假放得不久) or state the activity first as topic (這次放假放得不久).

dialogue.title: 在台灣旅行 · Traveling in Taiwan
dialogue.setting: 對話二 · Dialogue 2

text.traditional: 放假的時候，你去太魯閣了嗎？
text.simplified: 放假的时候，你去太鲁阁了吗？
text.pinyin: Fàngjià de shíhòu, nǐ qù Tàilǔgé le ma?
text.english: Did you go to Taroko during the vacation?

text.traditional: 我本來要去那裡，可是因為沒有車票了，所以後來決定去高雄玩。
text.simplified: 我本来要去那里，可是因为没有车票了，所以后来决定去高雄玩。
text.pinyin: Wǒ běnlái yào qù nàlǐ, kěshì yīnwèi méiyǒu chēpiào le, suǒyǐ hòulái juédìng qù Gāoxióng wán.
text.english: I originally intended to go there, but because there were no more train tickets, I later decided to go to Kaohsiung.

text.traditional: 高雄好玩嗎？
text.simplified: 高雄好玩吗？
text.pinyin: Gāoxióng hǎowán ma?
text.english: Was Kaohsiung fun?

text.traditional: 很好玩，我坐了三個半小時的火車，下了火車就坐捷運去西子灣了，那裡風景很漂亮。
text.simplified: 很好玩，我坐了三个半小时的火车，下了火车就坐捷运去西子湾了，那里风景很漂亮。
text.pinyin: Hěn hǎowán, wǒ zuò le sān ge bàn xiǎoshí de huǒchē, xià le huǒchē jiù zuò jiéyùn qù Xīzǐwān le, nàlǐ fēngjǐng hěn piàoliàng.
text.english: Very fun! I took the train for three and a half hours, and as soon as I got off the train, I took the MRT to Sizihwan. The scenery there was gorgeous.

text.traditional: 你應該搭高鐵去，這樣更快，只需要一個半小時。
text.simplified: 你应该搭高铁去，这样更快，只需要一个半小时。
text.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi dā gāotiě qù, zhèyàng gèng kuài, zhǐ xūyào yí ge bàn xiǎoshí.
text.english: You should have taken the High Speed Rail (HSR); it’s much faster, taking only an hour and a half.

text.traditional: 好，我下次一定要坐高鐵。你呢？這次旅行怎麼樣？
text.simplified: 好，我下次一定要坐高铁。你呢？这次旅行怎么样？
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ xià cì yídìng yào zuò gāotiě. Nǐ ne? Zhè cì lǚxíng zěnmeyàng?
text.english: All right, I'll definitely take the HSR next time. How about you? How was your trip?

text.traditional: 我玩得很開心，可是旅館的房間有點問題，浴室沒有水。
text.simplified: 我玩得很开心，可是旅馆的房间有点问题，浴室没有水。
text.pinyin: Wǒ wán de hěn kāixīn, kěshì lǚguǎn de fángjiān yǒudiǎn wèntí, yùshì méiyǒu shuǐ.
text.english: I had a great time, but there was a problem with the hotel room: the bathroom had no water.

text.traditional: 沒有水？那你怎麼洗澡？
text.simplified: 没有水？那你怎么洗澡？
text.pinyin: Méiyǒu shuǐ? Nà nǐ zěnme xǐzǎo?
text.english: No water? Then how did you take a shower?

text.traditional: 後來我換了房間，旅館老闆說付一半的錢就好了。
text.simplified: 后来我换了房间，旅馆老板说付一半的钱就好了。
text.pinyin: Hòulái wǒ huàn le fángjiān, lǚguǎn lǎobǎn shuō fù yíbàn de qián jiù hǎo le.
text.english: Later I changed rooms, and the hotel owner said paying half price was fine.

text.traditional: 合歡山下雪了嗎？冷不冷？
text.simplified: 合欢山下雪了吗？冷不冷？
text.pinyin: Héhuān Shān xiàxuě le ma? Lěng bù lěng?
text.english: Did it snow on Hehuanshan? Was it cold?

text.traditional: 下雪了，很冷，風也很大，可是很好玩。你看，這是我照的相片。
text.simplified: 下雪了，很冷，风也很大，可是很好玩。你看，这是我照的相片。
text.pinyin: Xiàxuě le, hěn lěng, fēng yě hěn dà, kěshì hěn hǎowán. Nǐ kàn, zhè shì wǒ zhào de xiàngpiàn.
text.english: It did snow. It was very cold, and the wind was strong, but it was really fun. Look, these are photos I took.

text.traditional: 你笑得好開心，風景真漂亮！
text.simplified: 你笑得好开心，风景真漂亮！
text.pinyin: Nǐ xiào de hǎo kāixīn, fēngjǐng zhēn piàoliàng!
text.english: You're smiling so happily, and the scenery is really beautiful!
